definitions.standard: The transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas state, without passing through the liquid state.
definitions.simple: When a solid directly turns into gas without becoming a liquid first, or a gas turns directly into a solid. Like dry ice making fog!
definitions.scientific: The transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas phase, or vice versa, without passing through the intermediate liquid phase. It is an endothermic phase transition.

examples: Dry ice turning into carbon dioxide gas
real_world_applications: Creating fog effects with dry ice

advanced_data.history: Historically used by alchemists to purify substances.

common_misconceptions: All solids melt into liquids first when heated. (Some, like camphor and ammonium chloride, sublime).
tutor_context.tutor_hint: Ask the student what happens to the white naphthalene balls they put in winter clothes. Do they leave a wet patch? No, they disappear completely into the air!
